AfterCardPlayed.maps_to: Relic.on_card_played (sts2_rl/relics/daughter_of_the_wind.py), dispatched per play iteration from CombatState._resolve_card_play (sts2_rl/combat.py) under the `not self.is_over` gate
AfterCardPlayed.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-07-28, and the second half of it was a MIS-DERIVATION in the original record rather than a sim defect. (a) G1, the per-CardPlay bracket, is genuinely fixed: `_resolve_card_play` opens `for play_index in range(play_count):` and fires `before_card_played` and `on_card_played` inside the body, mirroring CardModel.cs:1904's `for (int i = 0; i < playCount; i++)` with Hook.BeforeCardPlayed at :1929 and Hook.AfterCardPlayed at :1959; executed `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b04.py dotw` gives 1 Block alone and 2 Block with Throwing Axe, which is the C# answer. (b) G2 claimed the sim wrongly fires AfterCardPlayed once the combat has started ending. C# fires it too. `Hook.AfterCardPlayed` (Hook.cs:278-294) iterates `combatState.IterateHookListeners()` DIRECTLY, deliberately bypassing the IterateCombatHookListeners / IsOverOrEnding guard, and Hook.cs:275-276 states the reason verbatim: "Dispatched directly, not through the IterateCombatHookListeners guard: it completes resolution of the card that caused the kill." Its only gate is `if (CombatManager.Instance.IsInProgress)` (CardModel.cs:1957), and IsInProgress is still true between the killing blow and the teardown -- it is cleared only from CheckWinCondition (CombatManager.cs:1046-1059), which runs after the whole play action completes. So Daughter of the Wind DOES gain its 1 Block on the lethal Attack, and the sim's `not self.is_over` gate (the IsInProgress analogue) is the faithful one. RECORDED BECAUSE IT COST SOMETHING: a first pass at hook_dispatch/G8 changed this site to `is_over_or_ending` on the strength of the old G2 text and of test_hook_order.py's pin, which asserted the same wrong thing; that suppressed EVERY AfterCardPlayed listener on the winning card play -- including Game Piece's `DrawCmd.draw`, which can force a reshuffle and consume RNG, so it was stream-observable for the conformance exporter. The adversarial verification pass caught it, both sides were re-read at source, the change was reverted, and the pin was rewritten to assert the C# behaviour (test_after_card_played_still_fires_on_the_killing_blow). NOTE THE INVERSE MISMATCH, which is NOT this entry's and remains open: Hook.BeforeCardPlayed (Hook.cs:263-270) DOES go through IterateCombatHookListeners, and the sim does not gate it.  RECONCILED 2026-07-28 (Task 0, ledger-vs-code pass after the Tier 1 fix campaign): this entry was recorded `gap` against pre-campaign code and the divergence is closed today. The issue it replaced read: Rollup of guards G1 (CLOSED) and G2 (REWRITTEN, LIVE). The arithmetic and the type filter are right; the DISPATCH is still wrong, now in the opposite direction from the original recording.

CLOSED (G1): the hook bracket is per CardPlay. sts2_rl/combat.py:610 opens `for play_index in range(play_count):` and fires `self.hooks.before_card_played(card, played_target)` at :612 and `self.hooks.on_card_played(card, is_auto_play)` at :639 inside the body, mirroring CardModel.cs:1904's `for (int i = 0; i < playCount; i++)` with Hook.BeforeCardPlayed at :1929 and Hook.AfterCardPlayed at :1959. Executed (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b04.py dotw`): 1 Block alone, 2 Block with Throwing Axe — the C# answer.

LIVE (G2, rewritten 2026-07-28): the old G2 recorded that the sim wrongly fires AfterCardPlayed after the combat has started ending. That premise was a mis-derivation of Hook.cs. `Hook.AfterCardPlayed` (src/Core/Hooks/Hook.cs:272-294) is one of the eight dispatchers that deliberately BYPASS the IterateCombatHookListeners / IsOverOrEnding guard — it iterates `combatState.IterateHookListeners()` directly at :280 and :287, documented at :275-276 as "Dispatched directly, not through the IterateCombatHookListeners guard: it completes resolution of the card that caused the kill" (unlike Hook.BeforeCardPlayed at :263-270, which does go through the guard at :265). Its only gate is `if (CombatManager.Instance.IsInProgress)` at CardModel.cs:1957, and IsInProgress stays true between the killing blow and teardown: IsEnding (CombatManager.cs:171-202) is defined as "IsInProgress AND no primary enemy alive", and IsInProgress flips false only at CombatManager.cs:915/:962/:977, all reached from CheckWinCondition (CombatManager.cs:1046-1059), which ActionExecutor.cs:161-170 runs only after the entire play action completes. C# therefore GRANTS the 1 Block on the lethal Attack.

The sim now refuses it. sts2_rl/combat.py:638 gates the dispatch on `if not self.is_over_or_ending:`, and `is_over_or_ending` (combat.py:921-944) is `phase == COMBAT_OVER or player.is_dead or _all_enemies_dead()`. Executed today from the repo root: with daughter_of_the_wind and enemy hp=1, a Strike leaves `block = 0` (C# = 1); with hp=999, `block = 1`. The `player.is_dead` disjunct is correct (CardModel.cs:1950-1953 returns before the dispatch when the owner dies); the `_all_enemies_dead()` disjunct is the defect and must be dropped for this hook. The comment at combat.py:633-637 asserting "The C# test is `IsOverOrEnding`" contradicts CardModel.cs:1957 and Hook.cs:275-280 and is the only support for the gate.

No dual-mode split: `grep -n is_parity sts2_rl/combat.py` returns nothing, so the parity arm and the legacy/RL arm both suppress the dispatch. NOT dormant: the gate is shared machinery that drops EVERY AfterCardPlayed listener on the killing blow, including sts2_rl/relics/game_piece.py:19-23 (`DrawCmd.draw`, which can force a reshuffle and consume RNG), sts2_rl/relics/music_box.py (clone into a pile) and sts2_rl/relics/lost_wisp.py (damage to every living enemy) — so a conformance replay can desync on the winning card play. Separately, the inverse mismatch is now visible one line up: BeforeCardPlayed IS guard-routed in C# (Hook.cs:265) and is dispatched ungated at combat.py:612.  NARROWED 2026-07-28 (Task 0, ledger-vs-code pass after the Tier 1 fix campaign): the rest of this entry is closed in today's code. The issue it replaced read: Rollup of guards G1 (LIVE) and G2 per binding rule 4. The arithmetic and the type filter are right; the DISPATCH is not -- the sim fires on_card_played once per logical play where C# fires it once per CardPlay (G1), and fires it at all after the combat has started ending (G2).

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): Hook.AfterCardPlayed fires once per Replay ITERATION in C# and once per logical play in the sim, so a replayed Attack grants 1 Block instead of 2
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27, re-verified 2026-08-04 (line-shift only): the hook bracket is per CardPlay now. CombatState._resolve_card_play opens `for play_index in range(play_count)` and fires `hooks.before_card_played` INSIDE it (sts2_rl/combat.py:1153-1155, was :574-576) and `hooks.on_card_played` at the end of each iteration, gated on the combat still being in progress (sts2_rl/combat.py:1208-1209, was :597-600) -- CardModel.cs:1904-1965's `for (int i = 0; i < playCount; i++)` with Hook.BeforeCardPlayed at :1929 and Hook.AfterCardPlayed at :1957-1959. A replayed card therefore fires both hooks once per iteration, as in the game. WAS: combat.py bracketed the WHOLE play-count loop, so a Throwing-Axe-doubled card fired each hook once.

guards.what: G2 (RE-DERIVED 2026-08-04, was DORMANT gap): C# yields no listeners to a combat hook dispatched after the combat has started ending; the sim has no such gate, so a LETHAL Attack still grants its 1 Block
guards.issue: REVISED 2026-08-04: this guard entry was never re-synced after the hooks-level `AfterCardPlayed` entry above reconciled the same mechanism (2026-07-28) and is stale text left in the guards array, contradicting its own record. Its PREMISE is wrong: `Hook.AfterCardPlayed` does NOT go through `Hook.IterateCombatHookListeners` / the `IsOverOrEnding` guard at all -- it is one of eight dispatchers that deliberately bypass it (`Hook.cs:272-294`, documented at :275-276: "Dispatched directly, not through the IterateCombatHookListeners guard: it completes resolution of the card that caused the kill"). So C# DOES grant Daughter of the Wind's 1 Block on the lethal Attack -- the same conclusion the hooks-level `AfterCardPlayed` entry already reached, and the same one `test/test_hook_order.py::TestHookDispatchOrder::test_after_card_played_still_fires_on_the_killing_blow` pins (RE-RUN 2026-08-04: PASSES). The sim's current gate at combat.py:1208 (`if not self.is_over:`) is the faithful IsInProgress analogue, not a divergence. This entry's citation of `audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json` gap G8 as the 'named witness' was itself the mis-derivation the hooks-level entry above already flags -- G8 covers dispatchers that GO THROUGH the guarded path (AfterCardDrawn, AfterCardExhausted, AfterShuffle, AfterEnergySpent), which AfterCardPlayed does not; matching this relic's hook to G8 under binding rule 3 was the error, not a live/dormant call. If a reader still wants the general guarded-dispatcher shape, it lives at `hook_dispatch/G8` under one of ITS OWN witnesses, not this one.

guards.what: N1: BlockVar(1m, ValueProp.Unpowered) (DaughterOfTheWind.cs:16) passed to CreatureCmd.GainBlock (line 23) vs BLOCK = 1 with props=DamageProps.NON_CARD_UNPOWERED (daughter_of_the_wind.py:21, 30-33)
guards.rationale: Two things had to line up and both do. The CONSTANT: no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in the file, so 1 is the pinned non-ascension value. The PROP: DamageProps.NON_CARD_UNPOWERED is exactly ValueProp.UNPOWERED (valueprops.py:42), and BlockCmd.apply (cmds.py:456-494, was :130-151) -- re-verified 2026-08-04: per PROMPT.md bug class 27's fix, the dispatcher no longer gates modify_block_additive/multiplicative itself; each listener self-gates instead (DexterityPower.modify_block_additive, powers.py:247, refuses via `is_powered_card_or_monster_move_block(props)`), same OBSERVABLE result -- so the 1 Block is flat, which is what ValueProp.Unpowered means in the source. This matters: the relic fires on every Attack, so a Dexterity misclassification would compound all fight long. valueprops.py and cmds.py are hashed by this record (extra_sources).

guards.what: N2: `cardPlay.Card.Owner == base.Owner` (DaughterOfTheWind.cs:20) and the PlayerChoiceContext parameter (line 18)
guards.rationale: Both are the multiplayer per-player plumbing the shared contract puts out of scope: one player exists in the sim, so the owner clause is vacuous and the choice context has nothing to route. The clause the sim DOES keep, `Card.Type == CardType.Attack` (daughter_of_the_wind.py:28-29), is the only one that can vary.

guards.what: N3: Flash() and GainBlock's `fast: true` animation flag (DaughterOfTheWind.cs:22-23)
guards.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / FlashSfx / base.Status = RelicStatus.* / RefreshCounter / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.PreviewCardPileAdd are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter, sfx and hover text, and animation timing.
